options.text: The walls of the food pipe contract and relax in a wave-like motion that pushes the food forward.
The windpipe contracts and relaxes in waves to push the food into the stomach.
Food sliding down the food pipe makes its walls contract and relax in waves.
Wave-like propulsion occurs only in the food pipe, never elsewhere in the alimentary canal.

stem:
Aarav swallows a soft piece of banana. The food enters his food pipe (oesophagus) on its way to the stomach. Nearby is the windpipe. The walls of the food pipe can contract and relax in waves. Body position may be upright or upside down.

What moves the food down the food pipe?

teacher.key_rationale: Food-pipe walls push food by wave-like contraction and relaxation. The windpipe does not do that job; sliding food does not cause the waves; the same forward motion continues through the alimentary canal.
